plain_english: Thus the obligatory rite has been declared; now the occasional rite is stated.
sanskrit_cite: iti nityavidhiḥ prokto naimittikamathocyate

plain_english: When the fixed future obligatory rite is established, primacy and identification follow; therefore all is occasional.

plain_english: The wise call this occasional: sometimes arising, knower-determined existence.
sanskrit_cite: aśaṅkitavyāvaśyantāsattākaṃ jātucidbhavam pramātraniyataṃ prāhurnaimittikamidaṃ budhāḥ

plain_english: Twilight worship, occasion worship, and this thread offering are always obligatory because of their fixed form for all under scripture.
sanskrit_cite: sandhyādi parvasaṃpūjā pavitrakamidaṃ sadā nityaṃ niyatarūpatvātsarvasmin śāsanāśrite

plain_english: Knowledge, scripture, teacher, brother, and group attainments, birth rite differences, and own birth festival association are listed.

plain_english: Ancestral offering, calamity remedy, joy and wonder sight, yogini assembly, and meetings with own part and lineage are enumerated.

plain_english: Scripture explanation, city residence, endings, ordered emergence, deity vision, dream command, and vow expiation are listed.

sanskrit_cite: iti naimittikaṃ śrīmattantrasāre nirūpitam trayoviṃśatibhedena viśeṣārcānibandhanam

plain_english: There we speak of the occasion rite: it is twofold, kula and akula; the first was declared in the glorious yoga course.
sanskrit_cite: tatra parvavidhiṃ brūmo dvidhā parva kulākulam kulāṣṭakakṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ proktaṃ śrīyogasaṃcare

plain_english: Ocean moon and sage are thus for maheśi; first and fifteenth belong to brahma lineage, and two to kaumari.
sanskrit_cite: abdhīndu munirityetanmāheśyā brahmasantateḥ pratipatpañcadaśyau dve kaumāryā rasavahniyuk

plain_english: Ocean protector moon belongs to vaiṣṇavi; thirteenth to aindri; two to vārāhi; and a pair to caṇḍi.
sanskrit_cite: abdhirakṣīndu vaiṣṇavyā aindryāstvastraṃ trayodaśī vārāhyā randhrarudrau dve caṇḍyā vasvakṣiyugmakam

plain_english: Two lunar days belong to all; the tenth belongs to yogeśi, and the eighth also belongs to her, so it is proclaimed as two days.
sanskrit_cite: dve dve tithī tu sarvāsāṃ yogeśyā daśamī punaḥ tasyā apyaṣṭamī yasmāddvitithiḥ sā prakīrtitā

plain_english: Other akula occasions are marked in reverse; we speak of them as kula occasion as stated in bhairava kula.
sanskrit_cite: anyāścākulaparvāpi vaiparītyena lakṣitam kulaparveti tadbrūmo yathoktaṃ bhairave kule

plain_english: In haiḍara, in trika existence and trika kali kula etc., this breath-supported time was first declared in detail.

sanskrit_cite: sa cakrabhedasaṃcāre kāṃcit sūte svasaṃvidam svasaṃvitpūrṇatālābhasamayaḥ parva bhaṇyate

plain_english: Occasion means filling; or the word occasion has etymology from the root meaning filling, from that filling.

sanskrit_cite: haiḍare@tra ca śabdo@yaṃ dvidhā nāntetaraḥ śrutaḥ taccakracāraniṣṇātā ye kecit pūrṇasaṃvidaḥ

plain_english: Those joined in that assembly are devoted to that worship always; even one not identified worships at that time through own ordered worship.
sanskrit_cite: tanmelakasamāyuktāste tatpūjāparāḥ sadā yo@pyatanmaya eṣo@pi tatkāle svakramārcanāt

plain_english: From that yogini and siddha assembly one becomes identified, as in a spectacle seer consciousness becomes nondifferent.
sanskrit_cite: tadyoginīsiddhasaṅghamelakāt tanmayībhavet yathā prekṣaṇake tattaddraṣṭṛsaṃvidabheditām

plain_english: One immediately obtains ordered-risen full own consciousness by entering that, gained by yoga practice order.

plain_english: By that, various fruit is obtained there at that time by worship quickly, as one with long-held wealth makes festival eagerly.
sanskrit_cite: tena tattatphalaṃ tatra kāle saṃpūjayācirāt yathā ciropāttadhanaḥ kurvannutsavamādarāt

plain_english: He favors a guest who arrived knowing that time; thus yogini and siddha leaders act for good fruit accomplishment.

plain_english: Even diligent beings favor someone who recognizes the right time. Since this has already been explained, that general rule is enough here for the kula tradition.
sanskrit_cite: yatnavanto@pi tatkālābhijñaṃ tamanugṛhṇate uktaṃ ca tatra teneha kule sāmānyatetyalam

plain_english: O goddess, whichever mantra, yoga, or ritual sequence abides in someone's heart by the teacher's command becomes a source of accomplishment when it is carried out through worship.
sanskrit_cite: yasya yaddhṛdaye devi vartate daiśikājñayā mantro yogaḥ kramaścaiva pūjanāt siddhido bhavet

plain_english: O goddess, worship should be done according to kula conduct for the sake of accomplishment and liberation, and on fulfilment times the satiation offering is especially important.

plain_english: O fair-faced goddess, those who negligently fail to make satiation offerings to the teachers and deities are badly behaved, corrupt, and no better than bound beings.
sanskrit_cite: gurūṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca na kurvanti pramādataḥ durācārā hi te duṣṭāḥ paśutulyā varānane

plain_english: If daily worship has been missed, one must still worship on these fulfilment times. The wandering practice taught for gaining knowledge, power, and similar benefits is also connected with this.
sanskrit_cite: abhāvānnityapūjāyā avaśyaṃ hyeṣu pūjayet aṭanaṃ jñānaśaktyādilābhārthaṃ yatprakīrtitam

plain_english: The shakti sacrifice that has been taught, including rites of subjugation, attraction, and slaying, all succeed with ease on fulfilment days.

plain_english: The fulfilment time is defined in six ways, by general and special forms. Among these, the first and fifth days of the month are called auspicious days.
sanskrit_cite: tatsāmānyaviśeṣābhyāṃ ṣoḍhā parva nirūpitam māsasyādyaṃ pañcamaṃ ca śrīdinaṃ paribhāṣyate

plain_english: In both lunar fortnights, the fourth, eighth, and final days are declared the most general fulfilment times.
sanskrit_cite: turyāṣṭamānyabhuvanacaramāṇi dvayorapi pakṣayoriha sāmānyasāmānyaṃ parva kīrtitam

plain_english: If, on those same general fulfilment days, a future conjunction involving a planet and lunar mansion occurs, that twofold factor makes the day a general-special case.

plain_english: Shambhu taught that this classification becomes elevenfold in each case, and among cases of the same kind the excellent one is to be distinguished.
sanskrit_cite: sā caikādaśadhaikasminnekasminvibhunoditā sajātīyā tu sotkṛṣṭetyevaṃ śambhurnyarūpayat

plain_english: This verse gives a coded list of fortnight and planetary combinations used in the fulfilment-time scheme, pairing lunar markers with sequences of planets and luminaries.
sanskrit_cite: kṛṣṇayugaṃ vahnisitaṃ śrutikṛṣṇaṃ vahnisitamiti pakṣāḥ arkendujīvacandrā budhayugmendvarkakaviguruvidhu syāt

sanskrit_cite: paraphalguścaitramaghe tiṣyaḥ prākphalgukarṇaśatabhiṣajaḥ mūlaprājāpatye viśākhikā śravaṇasaṃjñayā bhāni

plain_english: This verse sets out coded calendrical markers together with specific times such as first night, midnight, daybreak, and midday for the ritual schedule.
sanskrit_cite: randhre tithyarkapare vasurandhre śaśivṛṣāṅkarasarandhrayugam prathamaniśāmadhyaniśe madhyāhnaśarā dinodayo madhyadinam

plain_english: At the appointed time called first night, in the months beginning with Margashirsha, the female messenger may be a maiden, a woman of low birth, or a courtesan, provided she is passionate and knows reality.

plain_english: When the after-sacrifice is carried out completely, following the sequence of hidden and open rules and the conduct of the initial sacrifice, it is indeed foremost in every ritual application.

plain_english: When the proper time for the after-sacrifice is available, one should make every effort to use it. But in the month of Ashvayuj there is no such special lunar-mansion and planetary time, so that month is excluded.

plain_english: The reckoning of time, lunar mansion, and planet has been explained for eleven months. In Phalguna, the twelfth day of the bright fortnight is declared as a special fulfilment time.
sanskrit_cite: velābhagrahakalanā kathitaikādaśasu māseṣu phālgunamāse śuklaṃ yatproktaṃ dvādaśīdinaṃ parva

plain_english: Here the foremost special factor is the conjunction involving the piercing of the prior lunar day. Day and night are divided into three parts, giving a first, middle, and last division.
sanskrit_cite: agratithivedhayogo mukhyatamo@sau viśeṣo@tra divasaniśe kila kṛtvā tribhāgaśaḥ prathamamadhyamāparavibhāgaḥ

plain_english: Within that threefold division, the best time for worship is when the foremost time-slot coincides with the right lunar mansion and planet, and the ritual circle aligns with them.

plain_english: On fulfilment times, the initial sacrifice and desire-driven rites can succeed through worship alone, provided the day, time-slot, lunar mansion, and planet are properly arranged and their gentle or fierce nature is taken into account.

plain_english: Having understood the nature of the timing, the foremost practitioner should perform the appropriate task. But what if the lunar mansion, planet, and lunar day fall outside the declared time for worship?

plain_english: Some say that if there is a conflict, one should ignore the special astrological factor and follow the conventional worship time. But our teachers disagree: here the lunar day is the decisive special factor, not the mere time-slot.
sanskrit_cite: tamanādṛtya viśeṣaṃ pradhānayetsāmayamiti kecit neti tvasmadguravo viśeṣarūpā hi tithiriha na velā

plain_english: The lunar day becomes fully clear through the moon portion and the clusters of sun-rays, measured by planets and stars.

plain_english: Therefore the lunar day is primary here, qualified by union of planets and stars, while time is not principal; thus speaks the supreme lord.

plain_english: The lunar day is worshipful because of its principal form; in the absence of white, they say black goat sacrifice indeed.
sanskrit_cite: tithistu pūjyā pradhānarūpatvāt śvetābhāve kṛṣṇacchāgālambhaṃ hi kathayanti

plain_english: What scripture states again about waves and so forth: even time-stated desired rule is indicated by primacy; and there, on the Pausha festival day.

plain_english: Having worshipped, meditated, and chanted at midnight, the command bears fruit for one who has gone outside; so in Magha, speech from the circle bears fruit.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtvārcanamardhaniśi dhyātvā japtvā bahirgatasya yathā ādeśaḥ phalati tathā māghe cakrādvacaḥ phalati

plain_english: Soon comes desired accomplishment: in five there is friendship, wealth, and union; in the circle place, enemy destruction arises from anger and stone splitting.
sanskrit_cite: acirādabhīṣṭasiddhiḥ pañcasu maitrī dhanaṃ ca melāpaḥ cakrasthāne krodhāt pāṣāṇasphoṭanena ripunāśaḥ

plain_english: Attainment of accomplished command to the path's end is said by the lord; in absence of star-planet union, time is considered, but the lunar day must necessarily be observed.
sanskrit_cite: siddhādeśaprāptirmārgāntaṃ kathyate vibhunā bhagrahayogābhāve velāṃ tu titheravaśyamīkṣeta

plain_english: That clear form indeed, of the lunar day's natural rise, would give following star, planet, lunar day, and time parts; but the day is all-limb beautiful.
sanskrit_cite: sā hi tathā sphuṭarūpā titheḥ svabhāvodayaṃ dadyāt bhagrahatithivelāṃśānuyāyi sarvāṅgasundaraṃ tu dinam

plain_english: If it could be obtained, then most special worship should be arranged in this; and not only desired, only this in avoidance, because it is said.
sanskrit_cite: yadi labhyeta tadāsminviśeṣatamapūjanaṃ racayet naca kāmyameva kevalametatparivarjane yataḥ kathitaḥ

plain_english: Break of convention: in the glorious Bhairava Kula wave scripture, corrupt, bad-conducted, animal-like indeed are those who do not know the festival.
sanskrit_cite: samayavilopaḥ śrīmadbhairavakula ūrmiśāstre ca duṣṭā hi durācārāḥ paśutulyāḥ parva ye na viduḥ

plain_english: Non-performance of the desired rite would never be sinful; there, for accomplishment of follow-up sacrifice, circle-sacrifice is determined.

plain_english: Image-sacrifice is thus called in the glorious Yogishvari doctrine: obligatory and occasional rite, which is said here by the great lord.
sanskrit_cite: mūrtiyāga iti prokto yaḥ śrīyogīśvarīmate nityaṃ naimittikaṃ karma yadatroktaṃ maheśinā

plain_english: Circle-sacrifice is primary everywhere, especially in desired rites, for a knower, yogi, man, or woman in this image-named context.
sanskrit_cite: sarvatra cakrayāgo@tra mukhyaḥ kāmye viśeṣataḥ jñānī yogī ca puruṣaḥ strī vāsminmūrtisaṃjñake

plain_english: In yoga, with effort, that should indeed be joined: the supreme vessel; from contact with that, fullness would be, in Traishirasa and so forth.

plain_english: By that, all that is offered and done, the three worlds moving and still, is for the knower or yogi; whoever gives or does.

plain_english: Even after initiation, declared food is Brahma, essence, Hari, consumer, Shiva; thus the knower uplifts even dog-cookers.

plain_english: Having become composed of all principles, if he eats, he is a practitioner; by mere feeding, ten million are fed.
sanskrit_cite: sarvatattvamayo bhūtvā yadi bhuṅkte sa sādhakaḥ tena bhojitamātreṇa sakṛtkoṭistu bhojitā

plain_english: Then, dear one, if the knower of principles in this would eat, count would not be known; thus says blessed Shiva.

plain_english: All food is Maya-composed; Shiva is consumer, and indeed I; who indeed knows thus is teacher and principle-crosser.
sanskrit_cite: bhojyaṃ māyātmakaṃ sarvaṃ śivo bhoktā sa cāpyaham evaṃ yo vai vijānāti daiśikastattvapāragaḥ

plain_english: Having seen him, god coming, the playing herbs in the house say: turned back today by us from the dense ocean of samsara.
sanskrit_cite: taṃ dṛṣṭvā devamāyāntaṃ krīḍantyoṣadhayo gṛhe nivṛttamadyaivāsmābhiḥ saṃsāragahanārṇavāt

plain_english: Having attained whose face, we shall go to the supreme state; others are drinkers; indeed upward, while prana and apana are downward-faced.
sanskrit_cite: yadasya vaktraṃ saṃprāptā yāsyāmaḥ paramaṃ padam anye@pānabhujo hyūrdhve prāṇo@pānastvadhomukhaḥ

plain_english: In that consumer, O goddess, even hundreds of families of the giver are quickly released from the ocean of hell-torture.
sanskrit_cite: tasminbhoktari deveśi dātuḥ kulaśatānyapi āśveva parimucyante narakādyātanārṇavāt

plain_english: In the glorious Nishatana it is also said: even from seeking narration, having reached inside the ear, having gone out from the teacher's mouth.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmanniśāṭane@pyuktaṃ kathanānveṣaṇādapi śrotrābhyantarasaṃprāpte guruvaktrādvinirgate

plain_english: Even a drinker of liquor, a thief, a killer of a brahmin, or one who violates the teacher's bed is freed at the very moment of death; only the body remains.

plain_english: Whether last-born or twice-born, child, old, or young, even a border-dweller who is a knower becomes a purifier of the land.
sanskrit_cite: antyajo vā dvijo vātha bālo vṛddho yuvāpi vā paryantavāsī yo jñānī deśasyāpi pavitrakaḥ

plain_english: There the god is present with the goddess and attendants; therefore, one should first honor the teacher who is skilled in knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: tatra saṃnihito devaḥ sadevīkaḥ sakiṅkaraḥ tasmātprādhānyataḥ kṛtvā guruṃ jñānaviśāradam

plain_english: One should perform the worship of his form; according to the Yogīśvarīmata, this is done during the thread offering, at śrāddha, and fully on festival days.
sanskrit_cite: mūrtiyāgaṃ carettasya vidhiryogīśvarīmate pavitrārohaṇe śrāddhe tathā parvadineṣvalam

plain_english: It should also be done at solar and lunar eclipses, at worldly festivals and celebrations, at marriages and the like, and during the sacrificial rites of brahmins.
sanskrit_cite: sūryacandroparāgādau laukikeṣvapi parvasu utsave ca vivāhādau viprāṇāṃ yajñakarmaṇi

plain_english: The form-worship should be performed at initiation, consecration, purification of observances, and for the sake of a desired aim; it is of five kinds.

plain_english: The five types are the single, the paired, the mixed, the circle-joined, and the hero-mingled. The single is done by teachers alone, and the mixed is done by teachers together with others.

plain_english: The paired worship is done with practitioners and others together with their wives; it is of two kinds, either through union with one's wife or through union with a courtesan who has been brought by payment.
sanskrit_cite: sādhakādyaiḥ sapatnīkairyāmalaḥ sa dvidhā punaḥ patnīyogāt krayānītaveśyāsaṃyogato@thavā

plain_english: The circle-women and other fitting partners in power-union will be explained later; worship joined with them becomes the circle-joined rite, which grants all fruits.

plain_english: The worship performed together with all is called the hero-mingled rite; the teacher should be in the center, and the group of teachers forms the surrounding circle.

plain_english: Outside there are three enclosures in due order, extending up to the pledged initiates; or all may be arranged in rows, but in every case the teacher is always in the middle.

sanskrit_cite: dvāreṣvaṣṭau granthayaḥ syuḥ kṛtvetthaṃ tu pavitrakam pūjayitvā mantrajālaṃ tatsthatvātmasthate tataḥ

plain_english: Having prepared the threads, one should do the confluence rite; then for a year one should meditate Bhairava, witness of holes.
sanskrit_cite: pavitrakāṇāṃ saṃpādya kuryātsaṃpātasaṃskriyām tataḥ saṃvatsaraṃ dhyāyedbhairavaṃ chidrasākṣiṇam

plain_english: Having given the full offering, O goddess, one should bow to mantra Bhairava; om, toward the lord who fills all rite faults, the vow.
sanskrit_cite: dattvā pūrṇāhutiṃ devi praṇamenmantrabhairavam oṃ samastakriyādoṣapūraṇeśa vrataṃ prati

plain_english: Whatever unmade or corrupt made, O son of Mother, all that is mine, O lord of gods, may perish by your grace.
sanskrit_cite: yatkiṃcidakṛtaṃ duṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ vā mātṛnandana tatsarvaṃ mama deveśa tvatprasādātpraṇaśyatu

plain_english: In every way, O lord of the ray wheel, salutation to you; be gracious to me; by this the invitation thread should be given to the god.
sanskrit_cite: sarvathā raśmicakreśa namastubhyaṃ prasīda me anena dadyāddevāya nimantraṇapavitrakam

plain_english: The teacher should then give offering to yogini field mothers: five-cow-products, oblation, and tooth-stick, by disciples all around.
sanskrit_cite: yoginīkṣetramātṝṇāṃ baliṃ dadyāttato guruḥ pañcagavyaṃ caruṃ dantakāṣṭhaṃ śiṣyaiḥ samantataḥ

plain_english: The teacher should sleep; rising early, do the daily rite; then, having worshipped the rite, gather the threads.
sanskrit_cite: ācārya nidrāṃ kurvīta prātarutthāya cāhnikam tato vidhiṃ pūjayitvā pavitrāṇi samāharet

plain_english: Join tooth-stick, clay, nurse, prosperous nurse, water, and ash in the five places.
sanskrit_cite: dantakāṣṭhaṃ mṛcca dhātrī samṛddhātrī sahāmbunā catuḥsamaṃ ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ bhasma pañcasu yojayet

plain_english: Place the five purifiers in order in the front, right, west, up, and left mouths within Shiva's range.
sanskrit_cite: prāgdakṣapaścimordhvasthavāmavaktreṣu vai kramāt pañcaitāni pavitrāṇi sthāpayecceśagocare

plain_english: Employ kusha fuel and the five cow products at Sharva's front; then offer the threefold food joined with left nectar.
sanskrit_cite: kuśedhma pañcagavyaṃ ca śarvāgre viniyojayet vāmāmṛtādisaṃyuktaṃ naivedyaṃ trividhaṃ tataḥ

plain_english: Give blood, wine, and various drinks; then perform oblation with great-earth-born flesh mixed with sesame.
sanskrit_cite: dadyādasṛk tathā madyaṃ pānāni vividhāni ca tato homo mahākṣmājamāṃsaistilayutairatho

plain_english: Alternatively use sesame with ghee, or rice with grains, along with sugar pieces soaked in the five nectars.
sanskrit_cite: tilairghṛtayutairyadvā taṇḍulairatha dhānyakaiḥ śarkarākhaṇḍasaṃyuktapañcāmṛtapariplutaiḥ

plain_english: Cast the root mantra a thousand and eight times, the flames a hundred and eight times, then the full offering.
sanskrit_cite: mūlaṃ sahasraṃ sāṣṭoktaṃ triśaktau brahmavaktrakam arciṣāṃ tu śataṃ sāṣṭaṃ tataḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ kṣipet

plain_english: Taking the purifier in the palms, recite this to the lord: whatever was done by me from desire or unwillingness.
sanskrit_cite: tato@ñjalau pavitraṃ tu gṛhītvā prapaṭhedidam akāmādathavā kāmādyanmayā na kṛtaṃ vibho

plain_english: May that flawless state be mine, O lord, through the purifier and your command; may the root mantra fulfill the rite rule.
sanskrit_cite: tadacchidraṃ mamāstvīśa pavitreṇa tavājñayā mūlamantraḥ pūrayeti kriyāniyamamityatha

plain_english: Give the purifier ending in vaushat, then in order three purifiers ending in nada, samana, and unmana.
sanskrit_cite: vauṣaḍantaṃ pavitraṃ ca dadyādbindvavasānakam nādāntaṃ samanāntaṃ cāpyunmanāntaṃ kramāttrayam

plain_english: The elemental practitioner gives the fourfold in direct order; the dedicated practitioner gives the fourfold purifier in reverse order.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ catuṣṭayaṃ dadyādanulomena bhautikaḥ naiṣṭhikastu vilomena pavitrakacatuṣṭayam

plain_english: Whatever various items such as clothes, umbrellas, ornaments, lamp garlands, and a gold sesame vessel are offered.
sanskrit_cite: yatkiñcidvividhaṃ vastracchatrālaṅkaraṇādikam tannivedyaṃ dīpamālāḥ suvarṇatilabhājanam

plain_english: For complete fulfillment, Shiva devotees are to be fed and worshipped according to ability, with a pair of cloths.
sanskrit_cite: vastrayugmayutaṃ sarvasampūraṇanimittataḥ bhojanīyāḥ pūjanīyāḥ śivabhaktāstu śaktitaḥ

plain_english: Perform the great festival for the specified month and day period; afterward they should never go to another place.
sanskrit_cite: catustridvyekamāsādidinaikāntaṃ mahotsavam kuryāttato na vrajeyuranyasthānaṃ kadācana

plain_english: The teacher is to be worshipped and given a new milk-giving cow adorned with gold, jewels, silver, and cloth.
sanskrit_cite: tatastu daiśikaḥ pūjyo gāmasmai kṣīriṇīṃ navām dadyātsuvarṇaratnādirupyavastravibhūṣitām

plain_english: The guru should say, "Your rite is complete," to be said for the god of gods and for his return.
sanskrit_cite: vadedguruśca saṃpūrṇo vidhistava bhavatviti vaktavyaṃ devadevasya punarāgamanāya ca

plain_english: Then dismissal is done; the guru takes the hidden ornaments and food offering for sacrifice and employs them.
sanskrit_cite: tato visarjanaṃ kāryaṃ guptamābharaṇādikam naivedyaṃ gururādāya yāgārthe tanniyojayet

plain_english: The common purifier of the four is remembered; no higher vow exists, and what praise of it is declared.
sanskrit_cite: caturṇāmapi sāmānyaṃ pavitrakamiti smṛtam nāsmādvrataṃ paraṃ kiñcit kā vāsya stutirucyate

plain_english: Do not cast the remainder into deep water flow; place it firmly. Then the occasional rite previously taught by me follows.
sanskrit_cite: śeṣaṃ tvagādhe vāryoghe kṣipenna sthāpayetsthiram atha naimittikavidhiryaḥ purāsūtrito mayā

plain_english: There, worship of the god is especially to be done, and the wheel sacrifice is to be performed by the wise according to the previously stated method.
sanskrit_cite: sa bhaṇyate tatra kāryā devasyārcā viśeṣataḥ cakrayāgaśca kartavyaḥ pūrvoktavidhinā budhaiḥ

plain_english: There, whatever helps desired enjoyment or liberation, whether by tradition or directly, and whether of conscious or unconscious self, qualifies.
sanskrit_cite: tatra yadyannijābhīṣṭabhogamokṣopakārakam pāramparyeṇa sākṣādvā bhaveccidacidātmakam

plain_english: That is worshipful; its means are worshipful for attaining identity with it, and means such as image, time, and rite are fully worshipped.
sanskrit_cite: tatpūjyaṃ tadupāyāśca pūjyāstanmayatāptaye tadupāyo@pi saṃpūjyo mūrtikālakriyādikaḥ

plain_english: Through its worship the means gains capacity; by becoming identical with its form, one quickly obtains the goal.
sanskrit_cite: upeyasūtisāmarthyamupāyatvaṃ tadarcanāt tadrūpatanmayībhāvādupeyaṃ śīghramāpnuyāt

plain_english: As there is non-proximity in the means, so inevitable task-ness follows, especially in worship and related rites.
sanskrit_cite: yathā yathā ca naikaṭyamupāyeṣu tathā tathā avaśyaṃbhāvi kāryatvaṃ viśeṣāccārcanādike

plain_english: When the acquisition of some knowledge that helps enjoyment and liberation is declared primary, the occasional day is declared primary by the wise.
sanskrit_cite: jñānasya kasyacitprāptirbhogamokṣopakāriṇaḥ yadā tanmukhyamevoktaṃ naimittikadinaṃ budhaiḥ

plain_english: The means to that knowledge is the scripture, and the teacher is a suitable speaker. Even a fellow disciple who knows that scripture can impart knowledge through dialogue.
sanskrit_cite: tadupāyaḥ śāstramatra vaktāpyaupayiko guruḥ tadvidyo@pi gurubhrātā saṃvādājjñānadāyakaḥ

plain_english: The teacher's wife, brother, son, and others belong to this group not because of birth relations, but because of their connection with knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: guroḥ patnī tathā bhrātā putra ityādiko gaṇaḥ na yonisaṃbandhavaśādvidyāsaṃbandhajastu saḥ

plain_english: Those established in body and ego through the development of seed and blood form a lineage that supports the body, and this is fully established among blood relatives.
sanskrit_cite: vīryāruṇaparīṇāmadehāhantāpratiṣṭhitāḥ dehopakārasantānā jñāteye pariniṣṭhitāḥ

plain_english: And so, in the traditional law texts, inheritance by lineage is indeed fitting, since it is determined by the distinction between nearer and more distant relations.
sanskrit_cite: tathāca smṛtiśāstreṣu santaterdāyahāritā yuktaiva tāvānsa hyukto bhedāddūrāntikatvataḥ

plain_english: But those who have abandoned attachment to the body and share in awareness and the sense of I enjoy kinship through two lineages that support awareness.
sanskrit_cite: ye tu tyaktaśarīrāsthā bodhāhambhāvabhāginaḥ bodhopakārasantānadvayātte bandhutājuṣaḥ

plain_english: In this regard, when one's seeing and acting are opened by the Lord's power, one understands that this body is indeed made from a series of earlier material causes.
sanskrit_cite: tatretthaṃ prāgyadā paśyecchaktyunmīlitadṛkkriyaḥ dehastāvadayaṃ pūrvapūrvopādānanirmitaḥ

plain_english: The self is free from change and, being eternal, has no cause; yet by its own freedom it remains as if concealed.
sanskrit_cite: ātmā vikārarahitaḥ śāśvatatvādahetukaḥ svātantryāt punarātmīyādayaṃ channa iva sthitaḥ

plain_english: And again, when it becomes manifest and attains the state of Bhairava, that manifestation is strongly characterized by both enjoyment and liberation.
sanskrit_cite: punaśca prakaṭībhūya bhairavībhāvabhājanam tatrāsya prakaṭībhāve bhuktimuktyātmake bhṛśam

plain_english: The suitable means for this is the lineage of knowledge, operating through a stream of such and similar knowledge that gradually becomes clear.
sanskrit_cite: ya upāyaḥ samucito jñānasantāna eṣa saḥ kramasphuṭībhavattādṛksadṛśajñānadhārayā

plain_english: As what is of a different kind fades away, the goal is quickly attained; in this way, even a knowledge lineage long accustomed to beginningless worldly life is transformed.
sanskrit_cite: galadvijātīyatayā prāpyaṃ śīghraṃ hi labhyate evaṃ cānādisaṃsārocitavijñānasantateḥ

plain_english: When that worldly lineage is destroyed, transcendent knowledge arises and takes on the character of another, noble lineage not accustomed to worldly life.
sanskrit_cite: dhvaṃse lokottaraṃ jñānaṃ santānāntaratāṃ śrayet asaṃsārocitodāratathāvijñānasantateḥ

plain_english: The primary and original cause is the teacher's knowledge entering the self, clearly bestowing its own distinctive qualities.
sanskrit_cite: kāraṇaṃ mukhyamādyaṃ tadguruvijñānamātmagam atyantaṃ svaviśeṣāṇāṃ tatrārpaṇavaśāt sphuṭam

plain_english: That knowledge is indeed a fitting material cause; for even when bodies differ, the difference and non-difference that apply to the bodily lineage do not apply in the same way to the lineage of knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: upādānaṃ hi tadyuktaṃ dehabhede hi satyapi dehasantatigau bhedābhedau vijñānasantateḥ

plain_english: It is not the same as a yogi animating a corpse-body by will; when a yogi brings life to another body and so on, that does not create the same kind of continuity, since the yogi does not abandon his own body.
sanskrit_cite: na tathātvāya yogīcchāviṣṭaśāvaśarīravat yoginaḥ paradehādijīvattāpādane nijam

plain_english: Even if a yogi, without abandoning the body, becomes the basis for various knowledges, that does not change the fact that the lineage of knowledge is primary over the bodily lineage.
sanskrit_cite: dehamatyajato nānājñānopādānatā na kim tena vijñānasantānaprādhānyādyaunasantateḥ

plain_english: Thus, when there is a mutual lineage of teachers established in the knowledge of Shiva, a threefold structure is recognized: a primary cause and an assisting cause.
sanskrit_cite: anyonyaṃ gurusantāno yaḥ śivajñānaniṣṭhitaḥ itthaṃ sthite trayaṃ mukhyaṃ kāraṇaṃ sahakāri ca

plain_english: Thus the teacher's group is understood in terms of cause and effect: the teacher is the cause, and his wife is the assisting cause.
sanskrit_cite: ekakāraṇakāryaṃ ca vastvityeṣa gurorgaṇaḥ guruḥ kāraṇamatroktaṃ tatpatnī sahakāriṇī

plain_english: Because one without power would not be eligible for ritual, the outer counterpart of the inner noble power of awareness is ordinarily required.
sanskrit_cite: yato niḥśaktikasyāsya na yāge@dhikṛtirbhavet antaḥsthodārasaṃvittiśakterbāhyāṃ vināpi tām

plain_english: Just as a yogi may have capacity even without an assisting cause, those born of one cause are brothers; and anyone similar to that may also be regarded in the same way.
sanskrit_cite: sāmarthyaṃ yogino yadvadvināpi sahakāriṇam ekajanyā bhrātaraḥ syustatsadṛgyastu ko@pi saḥ

plain_english: Again, the teacher group is also spoken of through lineage connection; but this primary lineage is always to be worshiped and honored.
sanskrit_cite: punaḥ paramparāyogādguruvargo@pi bhaṇyate mukhya eṣa tu santānaḥ pūjyo mānyaśca sarvadā

plain_english: For teachers and others, the days of birth, initiation, and death are significant, because each of these days is a cause connected with knowledge, the means, the body, and so on.
sanskrit_cite: gurvādīnāṃ ca sambhūtau dīkṣāyāṃ prāyaṇe@pi ca yadahastaddhi vijñānopāyadehādikāraṇam

plain_english: Thus one's own birthday is said to be a means of knowledge, because it is the cause of the body through which such enjoyment, liberation, and so on become possible.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ svajanmadivaso vijñānopāya ucyate tādṛgbhogāpavargādihetordehasya kāraṇam

plain_english: The day on which initiation or a similar consecration of one's self takes place should be regarded as a primary birthday, because it marks the birth of the knowledge lineage.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣādikaśca saṃskāraḥ svātmano yatra cāhni tat bhavejjanmadinaṃ mukhyaṃ jñānasantānajanmataḥ

plain_english: One's own death day will be an occasional observance for others, because at the time of death one becomes non-different from Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: svakaṃ mṛtidinaṃ yattu tadanyeṣāṃ bhaviṣyati naimittikaṃ mṛto yasmācchivābhinnastadā bhavet

plain_english: There we clearly speak of death's nature: even pervasive Shiva becomes contracted by the seal of self-willed creation.
sanskrit_cite: tatra prasaṅgānmaraṇasvarūpaṃ brūmahe sphuṭam vyāpako@pi śivaḥ svecchākḷptasaṅkocamudraṇāt

plain_english: By the flood of varied fruit-actions one becomes a body-taker; body-taking is thus tied to womb-body movement.
sanskrit_cite: vicitraphalakarmaughavaśāttattaccharīrabhāk śarīrabhāktvaṃ caitāvadyattadgarbhasthadehagaḥ

plain_english: When consciousness rises from the void, the first breath-arising occurs in womb-body making, and that lordship returns again.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvitteḥ śūnyarūḍhāyāḥ prathamaḥ prāṇanodayaḥ garbhasthadehanirmāṇe tasyaiveśvaratā punaḥ

plain_english: The uncontracted lord is called maker of body; he is wind-self in the firm body-machine, by consciousness-self.
sanskrit_cite: asaṅkocasya tanvādikartā teneśa ucyate sa vāyvātmā dṛḍhe tasmindehayantre cidātmanā

plain_english: Being driven, it moves like wind in a bellows; therefore it awakens like one risen from deep sleep.
sanskrit_cite: preryamāṇo vicarati bhastrāyantragavāyuvat ataḥ prāggāḍhasaṃsuptotthitavatsa prabuddhyate

plain_english: Gradually with the body breathing becomes stronger; even there, by action-destiny strength, breathing suffers injury.
sanskrit_cite: kramāddehena sākaṃ ca prāṇanā syādbalīyasī tatrāpi karmaniyatibalātsā prāṇanākṣatām

plain_english: It grasps from excess void-cavity consciousness touch; thus gradually the nourished body-breath becomes greatly strong.
sanskrit_cite: gṛhṇāti śūnyasuṣirasaṃvitsparśādhikatvataḥ evaṃ krameṇa saṃpuṣṭadehaprāṇabalo bhṛśam

plain_english: The womb-born body-goer enjoys pleasures made by action; this is said in the cave-named scripture by the cool-ray-crowned.
sanskrit_cite: bhogānkarmakṛtānbhuṅkte yonyayonijadehagaḥ uktaṃ ca gahvarābhikhye śāstre śītāṃśumaulinā

plain_english: As a householder dwells in a house he has made, so the embodied one, devoid of action-qualities, dwells in a body he has made.
sanskrit_cite: yathā gṛhaṃ viniṣpādya gṛhī samadhitiṣṭhati tathā dehī tanuṃ kṛtvā kriyādiguṇavarjitaḥ

plain_english: The mere flicker, even he, is called pre-partial; the clear senses principle is spoken of as whole-self.
sanskrit_cite: kiñcitsphuraṇamātraḥ prāgniṣkalaḥ so@pi śabdyate sphuṭendriyāditattvastu sakalātmeti bhaṇyate

plain_english: And so forth spoken by Gahvara; from that indeed read much; but when actions are destroyed, the body-machine goes otherwise.
sanskrit_cite: ityādi śrīgahvaroktaṃ tata eva paṭhedbahu kṣaye tu karmaṇāṃ teṣāṃ dehayantre@nyathāgate

plain_english: The breath-machine breaks apart; the body becomes like a wall; contraction and expansion in the nerve-wheels reverse.
sanskrit_cite: prāṇayantraṃ vighaṭate dehaḥ syātkuḍyavattataḥ nāḍīcakreṣu saṅkocavikāsau viparītataḥ

plain_english: Breaking, drying, moisture, wind, phlegm, fire decrease and increase, and such; whatever crushes the prior state.
sanskrit_cite: bhaṅgaḥ śoṣaḥ klidirvātaśleṣmāgnyapacayoccayaiḥ ityevamādi yatkiñcit prāksaṃsthānopamardakam

plain_english: The breaking of the body-machine is said by wise ones; when that machine breaks, consciousness-breathing becomes self-ness.
sanskrit_cite: dehayantre vighaṭanaṃ tadevoktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ tasminvighaṭite yantre sā saṃvitprāṇanātmatām

plain_english: It grasps in a womb-born or other body; in an action-painted body, that body awakens then like one risen from sleep.
sanskrit_cite: gṛhṇāti yonije@nyatra vā dehe karmacitrite sa dehaḥ pratibudhyeta prasuptotthitavattadā

plain_english: Even for that, enjoyment, destruction, and immortalities occur; creation, maintenance, and destruction arise from action strength.
sanskrit_cite: tasyāpi bhogataddhānimṛtayaḥ prāgvadeva hi visṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārā ete karmabalādyataḥ

plain_english: Therefore grace, for one following destiny, time, and variety, is that which blossoms in its own nature.
sanskrit_cite: ato niyatikālādivaicitryānuvidhāyinaḥ anugrahastu yaḥ so@yaṃ svasvarūpe vikasvare

plain_english: As knowledge-self, how does it await action-destiny and the like? Because of contracted life, action, time, and destiny await.
sanskrit_cite: jñaptyātmeti kathaṃ karmaniyatyādi pratīkṣate karmakālaniyatyādi yataḥ saṅkocajīvitam

plain_english: In the form of contraction-loss, how is the cause in grace? Grace is divided into gradual and intense.
sanskrit_cite: saṅkocahānirūpe@sminkathaṃ heturanugrahe anugrahaśca kramikastīvraśceti vibhidyate

plain_english: This was spoken in detail before; what need repetitions? By that, initiation and Shiva-knowledge burn the contraction bond.
sanskrit_cite: prāk caiṣa vistarātprokta iti kiṃ punaruktibhiḥ tena dīkṣāśivajñānadagdhasaṅkocabandhanaḥ

plain_english: At body-end, Shiva indeed; for him there is no staying in another body, even for those descended in truth and followers of Shankara's command.
sanskrit_cite: dehānte śiva eveti nāsya dehāntarasthitiḥ ye@pi tattvāvatīrṇānāṃ śaṃkarājñānuvartinām

plain_english: Dead in houses of self-born, sage, god, sage, man and other worlds, having reached that city, are initiated by city-lords gradually.
sanskrit_cite: svayambhūmunidevarṣimanujādibhuvāṃ gṛhe mṛtāste tatpuraṃ prāpya pureśairdīkṣitāḥ kramāt

plain_english: Having descended into mortal or not, they go to Shiva without rebirth; there self-born are in two ways, some devoted to grace.
sanskrit_cite: martye@vatīrya vā no vā śivaṃ yāntyapunarbhavāḥ tatra svayambhuvo dvedhā ke@pyanugrahatatparāḥ

plain_english: Some serve only the place of their own-duty-come part; among those commanded for grace, the man who dies.
sanskrit_cite: ke@pi svakṛtyāyātāṃśasthānamātropasevinaḥ ye@nugrahārthamājñaptāsteṣu yo mriyate naraḥ

plain_english: He goes to clear grace without mortal descent, and he who does his own task does not partially abandon that place.
sanskrit_cite: so@nugrahaṃ sphuṭaṃ yāti vinā martyāvatārataḥ yastu svakāryaṃ kurvāṇastatsthānaṃ nāṃśatastyajet

plain_english: As gauri practicing austerity in kashmir goes to a cave, or as narahari the lord is in meditation lift.
sanskrit_cite: yathā gaurī tapasyantī kaśmīreṣu guhāgatā tatraiva vā yathā dhyānoḍḍāre naraharirvibhuḥ

plain_english: Leading vitasta and frightening proud demons, risen in saligrama, as vishnu or shiva of self-enjoying.
sanskrit_cite: vitastāṃ nayato daityāṃstrāsayandṛpta utthitaḥ sāligrāme yathā viṣṇuḥ śivo vā svopabhoginaḥ

plain_english: Practicing austerity in badari, nara and narayana, and such gods are established in their own task portions.
sanskrit_cite: tapasyantau badaryāṃ ca naranārāyaṇau tathā ityevamādayo devāḥ svakṛtyāṃśasthitāstathā

plain_english: Worshiped gods quickly grant fitting fruit, and those established in their own task part who go to the end of the abode.
sanskrit_cite: ārādhitāḥ svocitaṃ tacchīghraṃ vidadhate phalam svakṛtyāṃśasthitānāṃ ca dhāmni ye@ntaṃ vrajanti te

plain_english: There, having enjoyed enjoyments, they descend among mortals; those descended become part-bearers and that again.
sanskrit_cite: tatra bhogāṃstathā bhuktvā martyeṣvavatarantyapi martyāvatīrṇāste tattadaṃśakāstanmayāḥ punaḥ

plain_english: By initiation, knowledge, practice and sequence they go to shiva selfhood; immobile and mobile animals, beasts in this duality, are dead.
sanskrit_cite: taddīkṣājñānacaryādikramādyānti śivātmatām sthāvarādyāstiryagantāḥ paśavo@smindvaye mṛtāḥ

plain_english: By purification of own action piercing that world, men and mere beasts taking variegation attain same world without discernment.
sanskrit_cite: svakarmasaṃskriyāvedhāttalloke citratājuṣaḥ puṃsāṃ ca paśumātrāṇāṃ sālokyamavivekataḥ

plain_english: Non-discernment, special unfolding from dullness, and thus immobile beings take increasing state, or.
sanskrit_cite: avivekastadviśeṣānunmeṣānmauḍhyatastathā sthāvarādyāstathābhāvamuttarottaratāṃ ca vā

plain_english: They do not attain direct rudra state; that gradually again, in swan and duck filled various tree thicket.
sanskrit_cite: prapadyante na te sākṣādrudratāṃ tāṃ kramātpunaḥ haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇe nānātarukulākule

plain_english: Thus this is said in scriptures; from that only in city city I speak field measure declared in auspicious all knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: ityetadāgameṣūktaṃ tata eva pure pure kṣetramānaṃ bruve śrīmatsarvajñānādiṣūditam

plain_english: From linga hundred hands field when teacher established self-born being; thousand but half when sage joined.
sanskrit_cite: liṅgāddhastaśataṃ kṣetramācāryasthāpite sati svayambhūte sahasraṃ tu tadardhamṛṣiyojite

plain_english: When truth-knower establishes linga, fruit is self-born-like; when non-truth-knower, then teacher establishes linga then.
sanskrit_cite: tattvavitsthāpite liṅge svayambhūsadṛśaṃ phalam atattvavidyadācāryo liṅgaṃ sthāpayate tadā

plain_english: Again rite becomes fault, indeed otherwise both corrupting: if opinion says I other, supreme self other, shiva other.
sanskrit_cite: punarvidhirbhaveddoṣo hyanyathobhayadūṣakaḥ ahamanyaḥ parātmānyaḥ śivo@nya iti cenmatiḥ

plain_english: Not liberates, not; liberated and all self-filled because; therefore by truth-knower whatever established linga is supreme.
sanskrit_cite: na mocayenna muktaśca sarvamātmamayaṃ yataḥ tasmāttattvavidā yadyatsthāpitaṃ liṅgamuttamam

plain_english: That only as abode, resort for enjoyment and liberation; said in shri ratnamala, knowing time arrived.
sanskrit_cite: tadevāyatanatvena saṃśrayedbhuktimuktaye uktaṃ śrīratnamālāyāṃ jñātvā kālamupasthitam

plain_english: Liberation seeker should not fear, should go abandon body without doubt; or deceive time in pilgrimage abode merits, beloved.
sanskrit_cite: mokṣārthī na bhayaṃ gacchettyajeddehamaśaṅkitaḥ tīrthāyatanapuṇyeṣu kālaṃ vā vañcayetpriye

plain_english: This path is of non-yogis; yogi should deceive by yoga; if incapable, being should go to field abode.
sanskrit_cite: ayogināmayaṃ panthā yogī yogena vañcayet vañcane tvasamarthaḥ san kṣetramāyatanaṃ vrajet

plain_english: In pilgrimage, from refuge of that, deception arises; by this and in earth etc, in principles by practice yoga.
sanskrit_cite: tīrthe samāśrayāttasya vañcanaṃ tu vijāyate anena ca dharādyeṣu tattveṣvabhyāsayogataḥ

plain_english: So far siddhi enjoying also said; for liberation field usefulness; in right knower account previously will be taught.
sanskrit_cite: tāvatsiddhijuṣo@pyuktā muktyai kṣetropayogitā samyagjñānini vṛttāntaḥ purastāttūpadekṣyate

plain_english: Of beasts this account; those initiated in that principle go to nearness to that lord by own fitness yoga.
sanskrit_cite: paśūnāmeṣa vṛttānto ye tu tattattvadīkṣitāḥ te tadīśasamīpatvaṃ yānti svaucityayogataḥ

plain_english: Born from fitness dependence, whose tendency where only, he there only should be appointed, from city lord upward purity sharer.
sanskrit_cite: yogyatāvaśasaṃjātā yasya yatraiva vāsanā sa tatraiva niyoktavyaḥ pureśāccordhvaśuddhibhāk

plain_english: Thus previously said auspicious; in auspicious svayambhuva also, who where desires enjoyments, he there only appointed.
sanskrit_cite: iti śrīpūrvakathitaṃ śrīmatsvāyambhuve@pica yo yatrābhilaṣedbhogānsa tatraiva niyojitaḥ

plain_english: Siddhi bearer, mantra power, etc., described elsewhere; those in principle knowledge, mantra, practice, etc.
sanskrit_cite: siddhibhāṅmantrasāmarthyādityādyanyatra varṇitam ye tu tattattvavijñānamantracaryādivartinaḥ

plain_english: When those knowers die, they attain union with that Rudra. Yet even after reaching that union, the form it takes varies according to their own latent impressions.
sanskrit_cite: mṛtāste tatra tadrudrasayuktvaṃ yānti kovidāḥ teṣāṃ sayuktvaṃ yātānāmapi saṃskārato nijāt

plain_english: In this way, descents that come from a portion of that Rudra can be highly varied. This is widely reported in the Siddhanta scriptures, in the Puranas, and elsewhere.
sanskrit_cite: tathā tathā vicitraḥ syādavatārastadaṃśataḥ siddhāntādau purāṇeṣu tathāca śrūyate bahu

plain_english: Even when all are equally descents of Rudra, their actions and experiences differ. This is because the form of any being is made up of many different powers.
sanskrit_cite: tulye rudrāvatāratve citratvaṃ karmabhogayoḥ anekaśaktikhacitaṃ yato bhāvasya yadvapuḥ

plain_english: A being is not something apart from its powers; it exists only as their collection. Therefore, what descends as a portion from Rudra and the rest is a particular configuration of powers.
sanskrit_cite: śaktibhyo@rthāntaraṃ naiṣa tatsamūhādṛte bhavet tena śaktisamūhākhyāt tasmādrudrādyadaṃśataḥ

plain_english: A portion descends so that the task suited to it can clearly be accomplished. The verse then turns to those who, after receiving initiation at a lower level, abandon their faith in it for something higher.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtyaṃ taducitaṃ siddhyet soṃ@śo@vatarati sphuṭam ye cādharaprāptadīkṣāstadāsthānujjhitāḥ pare

plain_english: Those who die fixed in that lower level still attain its highest reach. But those who let go of that elevation attain what lies above it.
sanskrit_cite: tattve mṛtāḥ kāṣṭhavatte@dhare@pyutkarṣabhāginaḥ ye tūjjhitatadutkarṣāste taduttarabhāginaḥ

plain_english: Even those initiated into a higher level, if they lack sufficient discernment, may reach only a lower end of it. Still, they partake of the fruit of that initiation.
sanskrit_cite: ye@pyūrdhvatattvadīkṣāste vinā tāvadvivekataḥ prāptādharāntā api taddīkṣāphalasubhāginaḥ

plain_english: Such people do not abandon their faith in that initiation, even if it rests on scriptural authority. Lacking discernment, they hold to it on the strength of scripture and common repute.
sanskrit_cite: atyaktāsthā hi te tatra dīkṣāyāmapi śāstritāt vinā vivekādāsthāṃ te śritā lokaprasiddhitaḥ

plain_english: The Supreme Lord taught that one who is merely a bound soul attains the same world, the initiated attains nearness, and one who is devoted to that path attains union.
sanskrit_cite: paśumātrasya sālokyaṃ sāmīpyaṃ dīkṣitasya tu tatparasya tu sāyujyamityuktaṃ parameśinā

plain_english: If someone who follows the higher teaching abandons faith in it through doubt, then even when going to its abode he obtains no fruit at all.
sanskrit_cite: yastūrdhvaśāstragastatra tyaktāsthaḥ saṃśayena saḥ vrajannāyatanaṃ naiva phalaṃ kiñcitsamaśnute

plain_english: On this point the God of gods said that for such a person initiation, knowledge, and even sacred places are in vain, and so on, as explained in detail elsewhere.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ tadviṣayaṃ caitaddevadevena yadvṛthā dīkṣā jñānaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ tasyetyādi savistaram

plain_english: Even if someone is unfit at first, if he remains steadfast in the abode of Shiva, then through that enduring bond of faith he will later obtain that very fruit.
sanskrit_cite: yastu tāvadayogyo@pi tathāste sa śivālaye paścādāsthānibandhena tāvadeva phalaṃ bhajet

plain_english: Merit gained from places like rivers, mountains, and pools is not the highest thing at death. Those who die with that merit enjoy the pleasures of heaven.
sanskrit_cite: nadīnagahradaprāyaṃ yacca puṇyaṃ na tanmṛtau utkṛṣṭaṃ tanmṛtānāṃ tu svargabhogopabhogitā

plain_english: Those who had gained knowledge and discernment, but near death take refuge in lower abodes, become veiled there.
sanskrit_cite: ye punaḥ prāptavijñānavivekā maraṇāntike adharāyataneṣvāsthāṃ śritāste@tra tirohitāḥ

plain_english: This is described as a defilement of their knowledge and may indeed count as sin. The established view is that it is removed through the proper sequence of initiation into the lords of those respective realms.
sanskrit_cite: tajjñānadūṣaṇoktaṃ yatteṣāṃ syātkila pātakam tattatpureśadīkṣādikramānnaśyediti sthitiḥ

plain_english: But those who, in mind and conduct, defile initiation, sacred abodes, and knowledge all go to hell.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣāyatanavijñānadūṣiṇo ye tu cetasā ācaranti ca tatte@tra sarve nirayagāminaḥ

plain_english: The loss of one's bond of faith in knowledge, sacred abodes, and initiation is to be recognized by disturbed activities, and those activities are of two kinds.
sanskrit_cite: jñānāyatanadīkṣādāvāsthābandhaparicyutiḥ vyāpāravyāhṛtairjñeyā tānyapi dvividhāni ca

plain_english: Some disturbances never arise when a person is healthy and appear only in illness, caused by bodily imbalance. These amount only to the experience of that condition.
sanskrit_cite: yāni jātucidapyeva svāsthye nodamiṣanpunaḥ asvāsthye dhātudoṣotthānyeva tadbhogamātrakam

plain_english: Bodily imbalance may awaken old worldly impressions, and they may slip in through temporary openings. But if they have mostly been burned by knowledge, they cannot grow again.
sanskrit_cite: dhātudoṣācca saṃsārasaṃskārāste prabodhitāḥ chidragā api bhūyiṣṭhajñānadagdhā na rohiṇaḥ

plain_english: But in those oriented toward isolation, some impressions never appear in good health and yet open up in illness. These arise from the descent of power.
sanskrit_cite: ye tu kaivalyabhāgīyāḥ svāsthye@nunmiṣitāḥ sadā asvāsthye conmiṣantyete saṃskārāḥ śaktipātataḥ

plain_english: Ordinary worldly impressions are formed by long, deep habituation from the past. As the Lord of Serpents said in the sutra, they appear in those openings.
sanskrit_cite: yataḥ sāṃsārikāḥ pūrvagāḍhābhyāsopasaṃskṛtāḥ ityūce bhujagādhīśastacchidreṣviti sūtrataḥ

plain_english: In those oriented toward isolation, some cognitions arise that were never practiced before. Because of the nature of transmigration, these cannot come from habit and must come from the descent of power.
sanskrit_cite: ye tu kaivalyabhāgīyāḥ pratyayāste na jātucit abhyastāḥ saṃsṛterbhāvāttenaite śaktipātataḥ

plain_english: These disturbed activities, when aggravated by bodily imbalance, lack settled certainty and reflective awareness, and they resemble the behavior of someone asleep or intoxicated.
sanskrit_cite: vyāpāravyāhṛtaistena dhātudoṣaprakopitaiḥ aprāptaniścayāmarśaiḥ suptamattopamānakaiḥ

plain_english: Even if disturbed behavior seems perverse and appears to defile knowledge, initiation, or the teacher, it should not be taken as true veiling when it has not taken root in the heart.
sanskrit_cite: viparītairapi jñānadīkṣāgurvādidūṣakaiḥ tirobhāvo na vijñeyo hṛdaye rūḍhyabhāvataḥ

plain_english: For this very reason, even an awakened person, while still in the body, may undergo karma-born experiences at death, such as visions of Yama's servants, snakes, and the like.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva prabuddho@pi karmotthānbhogarūpiṇaḥ yamakiṅkarasarpādipratyayāndehago bhajet

plain_english: This alone does not mean he is not liberated, for death is an experience just like birth and ongoing life. Therefore death can be of two kinds, involving pain or pleasure.
sanskrit_cite: naitāvatā na mukto@sau mṛtirbhogo hi janmavat sthitivacca tato duḥkhasukhābhyāṃ maraṇaṃ dvidhā

plain_english: So, just as the varied pleasures and pains of life do not destroy the liberated state of an awakened person, those same kinds of experiences at death do not destroy it either.
sanskrit_cite: ato yathā prabuddhasya sukhaduḥkhavicitratāḥ sthitau na ghnanti muktatvaṃ maraṇe@pi tathaiva tāḥ

plain_english: But those yogins who have become well established in a particular principle fix their mind on that very principle and, without doubt, go to it.
sanskrit_cite: ye punaryoginaste@pi yasmiṃstattve subhāvitāḥ cittaṃ niveśayantyeva tattattvaṃ yāntyaśaṅkitāḥ

plain_english: This is stated in the revered Svacchanda Tantra, beginning with the teaching about those who die through concentration on fragrance, and likewise the Malini scripture gives the fruits of the various concentrations.
sanskrit_cite: śrīsvacchande tataḥ proktaṃ gandhadhāraṇayā mṛtāḥ ityādi mālinīśāstre dhāraṇānāṃ tathā phalam

plain_english: For those who quickly abandon the body through concentrations, as if entering another body, there is no experience that can properly be called death.
sanskrit_cite: eteṣāṃ maraṇābhikhyo bhogo nāsti tu ye tanum dhāraṇābhistyajantyāśu paradehapraveśavat

plain_english: The ordinary experience of death consists in a cutting shock at the vital points, delusion spreading through the senses, and a mental sinking into darkness. None of this is found in these yogins.
sanskrit_cite: etāvānmṛtibhogo hi marmacchinmūḍhatākṣagā dhvāntābilatvaṃ manasi taccaiteṣu na vidyate

plain_english: For the yogin maintains mental effort, establishing an I-sense in another body, as long as the movement of intellect continues there.
sanskrit_cite: tathāhi mānasaṃ yatnaṃ tāvatsamadhitiṣṭhati ahaṃrūḍhyā pare dehe yāvatsyādbuddhisaṃcaraḥ

plain_english: The circle of breath, dependent on that same process, moves along the path, and by that very means the circle of senses in the other body becomes awakened.
sanskrit_cite: prāṇacakraṃ tadāyattamapi saṃcarate pathā tenaivātaḥ prabuddhyeta paradehe@kṣacakrakam

plain_english: Just as bees rise when the bee-king rises and settle when he settles, so all the activities of the senses follow the mind.
sanskrit_cite: makṣikā makṣikārājaṃ yathotthitamanūtthitāḥ sthitaṃ cānuviśantyevaṃ cittaṃ sarvākṣavṛttayaḥ

plain_english: Therefore, when he moves into another body, there is no inward merging of the senses as in ordinary death. Instead, a subtle continuity arises again, like a body.
sanskrit_cite: ato@sya paradehādisaṃcāre nāsti melanam akṣāṇāṃ madhyagaṃ sūkṣmaṃ syādetaddehavatpunaḥ

plain_english: Thus, for yogins who move into other bodies and likewise for those who move within bodies formed of various principles, there is no delusion.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ paraśarīrādicāriṇāmiva yoginām tattattattvaśarīrāntaścāriṇāṃ nāsti mūḍhatā

plain_english: These yogins should be known as twofold: worldly and initiated. The former become Shiva gradually, while the latter do so merely through experiencing that state.
sanskrit_cite: te cāpi dvividhā jñeyā laukikā dīkṣitāstathā pūrve śivāḥ syuḥ kramaśaḥ pare tadbhogamātrataḥ

plain_english: Initiation, being divided by many higher and lower distinctions, yields varied fruits for yogins.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣāpyūrdhvādharānekabhedayojanikāvaśāt bhidyamānā yogināṃ syādvicitraphaladāyinī

plain_english: But those who are knowers are of two kinds, according to whether their knowledge trembles or not. Among them, those whose knowledge trembles clearly become Shiva at the end of the body.
sanskrit_cite: ye tu vijñāninaste@tra dvedhā kampretaratvataḥ tatra ye kampravijñānāste dehānted śivāḥ sphuṭam

plain_english: Because knowledge has arisen in them, but it is not very clear due to association with other conceptual thoughts, nor is it uprooted in its nature.
sanskrit_cite: yato vijñānameteṣāmutpannaṃ naca susphuṭam vikalpāntarayogena nacāpyunmūlitātmakam

plain_english: Therefore, the conceptual thought that arises in the body from carelessness necessarily perishes when the body falls, and that supreme knowledge is then recognized.
sanskrit_cite: ato dehe pramādottho vikalpo dehapātataḥ naśyedavaśyaṃ taccāpi budhyate jñānamuttamam

plain_english: That knowledge, not destroyed within but standing as latent conceptual traces, having reached ripeness, indeed shines forth when the obstruction is removed.
sanskrit_cite: saṃskārakalpanātiṣṭhadadhvastīkṛtamantarā prāptapākaṃ saṃvarīturapāye bhāsate hi tat

plain_english: But those whose nature is well-practiced knowledge, who are always of the nature of Shiva, are indeed liberated while living; for them there is no question at all at the time of death.
sanskrit_cite: ye tu svabhyastavijñānamayāḥ śivamayāḥ sadā jīvanmuktā hi te naiṣāṃ mṛtau kāpi vicāraṇā

plain_english: For just as there is no question about the living-liberated being happy, unhappy, or deluded while they live, so too there is no such question at death.
sanskrit_cite: yathāhi jīvanmuktānāṃ sthitau nāsti vicāraṇā sukhiduḥkhivimūḍhatve, mṛtāvapi tathā na sā

plain_english: The Supreme Lord said this in the holy Ratnamala scripture, and so did the Lord Ahi, bearer of the burden of supporting the universe, in his own scripture.
sanskrit_cite: śrīratnamālāśāstre taduvāca parameśvaraḥ svaśāstre cāpyahīśāno viśvādhāradhurandharaḥ

plain_english: Whether in a street, amid urine and feces, in an outcaste's house, in hell, or in a cremation ground, whether with thought or without thought, the knower obtains liberation at the end.
sanskrit_cite: rathyāntare mūtrapurīṣamadhye caṇḍālagehe niraye śmaśāne sacintako vā gatacintako vā jñānī vimokṣaṃ labhate@pi cānte

plain_english: The words 'even' and 'also' indicate his state of living liberation; the mention of being with thought or without thought refers only to a possible circumstance at that time.
sanskrit_cite: apiceti dhvanirjīvanmuktatāmasya bhāṣate sacintācintakatvoktiretāvatsaṃbhavasthitim

plain_english: Whether at a holy place or in an outcaste's house, even if memory is lost, one who abandons the body, being liberated simultaneously with knowledge, attains absolute freedom, with sorrow destroyed.
sanskrit_cite: tīrthe śvapacagṛhe vā naṣṭasmṛtirapi parityajeddeham jñānasamakālamuktaḥ kaivalyaṃ yāti hataśokaḥ

plain_english: The Ananta-verses say that one might suspect good or bad deeds to bind him, but in fact they do not bind him.
sanskrit_cite: anantakārikā caiṣā prāhedaṃ bandhakaṃ kila sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ cāsya śaṅkyaṃ taccāsya no bhavet

plain_english: From the word 'even' one might think death with memory intact is possible, but death usually involves lost memory; and if memory was lost before death, what does that matter?
sanskrit_cite: apiśabdādaluptasmṛtyā vā saṃbhāvyate kila mṛtirnaṣṭasmṛtereva mṛteḥ prāk sāstu kiṃ tayā

plain_english: The optative indicates mere possibility, and the time-expression shows that death is not the cause of liberation.
sanskrit_cite: liṅca saṃbhāvanāyāṃ syādiyatsaṃbhāvyate kila saca kāladhvaniḥ prāha mṛtermuktāvahetutām

plain_english: Although 'isolation' may raise doubt because a body remains, that body no longer produces difference, so sorrowlessness is established.
sanskrit_cite: kaivalyamiti cāśaṅkāpadaṃ yāpyabhavattanuḥ bhedapradatvenaiṣāpi dhvastā tena viśokatā

plain_english: Just as connection with other bodies does not differentiate him, so too connection with his own body does not differentiate the living-liberated person.
sanskrit_cite: paradehādisaṃbandho yathā nāsya vibhedakaḥ tathā svadehasaṃbandho jīvanmuktasya yadyapi

plain_english: Therefore, for one who is non-different from Śiva and has set aside all universal forms, there is no real difference whether he is in a body or not.
sanskrit_cite: ataśca na viśeṣo@sya viśvākṛtinirākṛteḥ śivābhinnasya dehe vā tadabhāve@pi vā kila

plain_english: Even so, because suspicion based on old impressions of difference may persist, the text now speaks of aloneness; or else it does so from another standpoint.
sanskrit_cite: tathāpi prācyatadbhedasaṃskārāśaṅkanasthiteḥ adhunoktaṃ kevalatvaṃ yadvā mātrantarāśrayāt

plain_english: Those things do not know him as different, and he is not known as different by them; such a one is called liberated. The revered Traiśirasa also speaks of a state beyond the pair of sun and moon.
sanskrit_cite: tānyenaṃ na vidurbhinnaṃ taiḥ sa mukto@bhidhīyate śrīmattraiśirase@pyuktaṃ sūryendupuṭavarjite

plain_english: It is a state where disgust and its opposite are broken, steady on all sides like a pillar, free from all calamity, and beyond valid cognition and mental constructs.
sanskrit_cite: jugupsābhāvabhaṅgasthe sarvataḥ stambhavatsthite sarvavyāpattirahite pramāṇapratyayātige

plain_english: Absorbed in that inner awareness, one may still act yet remain unstained. The key example is space in a pot: even when the pot is broken, space is not destroyed.
sanskrit_cite: tasminbodhāntare līnaḥ karmakartāpyanañjanaḥ pradhānaṃ ghaṭa ākāśa ātmā maṣṭe ghaṭe@pi kham

plain_english: Just as space does not perish when the pot is broken, so this self does not perish; the knower becomes Śiva-natured, independent, and extends into all things.
sanskrit_cite: na naśyettadvadevāsāvātmā śivamayo bhavet svatantro@vasthito jñānī prasaretsarvavastuṣu

plain_english: For him there is neither mere being nor non-being, neither fixed form nor mental construction. This same point was spoken by the teacher in the Gītā.
sanskrit_cite: tasya bhāvo nacābhāvaḥ saṃsthānaṃ naca kalpanā etadevāntarāgūrya gururgītāsvabhāṣata

plain_english: Whatever state one remembers while leaving the body at the end, that alone one attains, because one has always been shaped by dwelling on that state.
sanskrit_cite: yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram taṃ tamevaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ

plain_english: Therefore remember me at all times and fight. When sattva is predominant, the one who dissolves then goes upward.
sanskrit_cite: tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu māmanusmara yudhya ca yadā sattve vivṛddhe tu pralīnastvūrdhvagastadā

plain_english: If one dissolves in rajas and tamas, one goes deluded into a karmic birth; then there is confusion of the senses and distress marked by labored breathing.
sanskrit_cite: kramādrajastamolīnaḥ karmayonivimūḍhagaḥ tatrendriyāṇāṃ saṃmohaśvāsāyāsaparītatā

plain_english: Experiences like these occur in the body and are not the same as abandoning the body; the real abandonment is only that single final moment consisting of the last breath.
sanskrit_cite: ityādimṛtibhogo@yaṃ dehe na tyajanaṃ tanoḥ yastvasau kṣaṇa evaikaścaramaḥ prāṇanātmakaḥ

plain_english: The instant immediately after which the body becomes like wood or a wall is the fractional moment of abandoning the body, the moment that separates one from it.

sanskrit_cite: yadvā niḥsukhaduḥkhādi yadi vānandarūpakam kasmādeti tadevaiṣa yataḥ smarati saṃvidi

sanskrit_cite: prāk prasphuredyadadhikaṃ deho@sau cidadhiṣṭhiteḥ yadeva prāgadhiṣṭhānaṃ citā tādātmyavṛttitaḥ

sanskrit_cite: vedyānāṃ kintu dehasya nityāvyabhicaritvataḥ sā ca tasyaiva dehasya pūrvamṛtyantajanmanā

plain_english: By memory, whose impressions come from past experience, Kallata our lineage teacher reasons thus.
sanskrit_cite: smṛtyā prācyānubhavanakṛtasaṃskāracitrayā yuktyānayāsmatsantānaguruṇā kallaṭena yat

plain_english: In bodily indistinction, breath-firmness is stated as the cause; otherwise, what is the cause of breath-firmness?
sanskrit_cite: dehāviśeṣe prāṇākhyadārḍhyaṃ heturudīritam tadyuktamanyathā prāṇadārḍhye ko heturekataḥ

sanskrit_cite: dehatvasyāviśeṣe@pītyeṣa praśno na śāmyati smaranniti śatā hetau tadrūpaṃ pratipadyate

plain_english: The body is remembered before because it was previously established and shining; therefore final remembering occurs in all-knowing mothers.
sanskrit_cite: prāk smaryate yato dehaḥ prākcitādhiṣṭhitaḥ sphuran ataḥ smaraṇamantyaṃ yattadasarvajñamātṛṣu

plain_english: Determination of another body is never accessible; clear memory of relatives, drinks, and so forth does not prove it.
sanskrit_cite: na jātu gocaro yasmāddehāntaraviniścayaḥ yattu bandhupriyāputrapānādismaraṇaṃ sphuṭam

sanskrit_cite: na taddehāntarāsaṅgi na tadantyaṃ yato bhavet kasyāpi tu śarīrānte vāsanā yā prabhotsyate

sanskrit_cite: dehasattve tadaucityājjāyetānubhavaḥ sphuṭaḥ yathā purāṇe kathitaṃ mṛgapotakatṛṣṇayā

sanskrit_cite: muniḥ ko@pi mṛgībhāvamabhyuvāhādhivāsitaḥ tatra so@nubhavo heturna janmāntarasūtaye

plain_english: His latent impression is the cause, like crow and palm; he remembers that very thing, as is always said.
sanskrit_cite: tasyaitadvāsanā hetuḥ kākatālīyavat sa tu nanu kasmāttadevaiṣa smarati ityāha yatsadā

plain_english: Shaped by that state, he remembers that very thing; thus I am, I will be, and that state is called becoming.
sanskrit_cite: tadbhāvabhāvitastena tadevaiṣa smaratyalam evamasmi bhaviṣyāmītyeṣa tadbhāva ucyate

plain_english: Becoming of the future is imagined, never of what exists; imagination is declared as gradual making clear.
sanskrit_cite: bhaviṣyato hi bhavanaṃ bhāvyate na sataḥ kvacit kramātsphuṭatvakaraṇaṃ bhāvanaṃ parikīrtyate

plain_english: Experience of the clear is not imagination; this is clear, as with a newborn child, animal, insect, or tree.
sanskrit_cite: sphuṭasya cānubhavanaṃ na bhāvanamidaṃ sphuṭam tadaharjātabālasya paśoḥ kīṭasya vā taroḥ

sanskrit_cite: mūḍhatve@pi tadānīṃ prāgbhāvanā hyabhavatsphuṭā sā tanmūḍhaśarīrānte saṃskārapratibodhanāt

plain_english: Through the gate of memory, latent impressions, even across separation of place and so forth, give the result of that body's variety.
sanskrit_cite: smṛtidvāreṇa taddehavaicitryaphaladāyinī deśādivyavadhāne@pi vāsanānāmudīritāt

plain_english: Because memory and impression have immediacy and one form, by such ascent of experience, even clear experience is imagined.
sanskrit_cite: ānantaryaikarūpatvātsmṛtisaṃskārayorataḥ tathānubhavanārūḍhyā sphuṭasyāpi tu bhāvitā

plain_english: Being imagined produces a body similar to that lineage, together with such relatives, sons, friends, and so forth.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvyamānā na kiṃ sūte tatsantānasadṛgvapuḥ tattādṛktādṛśairbandhuputramitrādibhiḥ saha

sanskrit_cite: bhāsate@pi pare loke svapnavadvāsanākramāt nanu mātrantarairbandhuputrādyaistattathā na kim

plain_english: This is known; he said it and knows for now. Let it be known in the crowd of activity and utterance, in the group of other mothers.
sanskrit_cite: vedyate ka idaṃ prāha sa tāvadveda vedyatām vyāpāravyāhṛtivrātavedye mātrantaravraje

plain_english: In dream he is not; this statement lacks speech and proof, while these are seen awake by me.
sanskrit_cite: svapne nāsti sa ityeṣā vākpramāṇavivarjitā ya evaite tu dṛśyante jāgratyete mayekṣitāḥ

plain_english: Let it be dream; this is false by the force of cognizer speech, for I see in dream, but no cognizers.
sanskrit_cite: svapna ityastu mithyaitattatpramātṛvacobalāt yānapaśyamahaṃ svapne pramātṝṃste na kecana

plain_english: They neither grieve nor see me; what proof is here, because all inferences rest in self-experience.

plain_english: Existence of another cognizer rests in consciousness, not located in that; existence of pot and so forth rests in consciousness, not located in that.

sanskrit_cite: tadvanmātrantare@pyeṣā saṃvinniṣṭhā na tadgatā tena sthitamidaṃ yadyadbhāvyate tattadeva hi

plain_english: At the end of the body, awakening occurs; if not, such awakening would not be possible, for in the final moment one purified by hearing brahma-knowledge awakens.
sanskrit_cite: dehānte budhyate no cet syādanyādṛkprabodhanam tathāhyantyakṣaṇe brahmavidyākarṇanasaṃskṛtaḥ

plain_english: The creature is liberated, as said, from the strength of prior impressions, through particles, inner word, remembrance, and the fourth end.
sanskrit_cite: mucyate janturityuktaṃ prāksaṃskārabalatvataḥ nipātābhyāmantaśabdātsmaraṇācchaturantyataḥ

plain_english: From a quarter, from a whole half-verse, from what immediately follows, and from the absorbed word, all that stated meaning is true reality.
sanskrit_cite: pādācca nikhilādardhaślokācca samanantarāt līnaśabdācca sarvaṃ taduktamarthasatattvakam

plain_english: Not knowing this, however, all who cling to kusha and kasha vary; some follow one order, some another.
sanskrit_cite: ajñātvaitattu sarve@pi kuśakāśāvalambinaḥ yattadorvyatyayaṃ kecitkecidanyādṛśaṃ kramam

plain_english: They abandon two different orders and particles, and explain the seventh case; all that is not suitable in joining.
sanskrit_cite: bhinnakramau nipātau ca tyajatīti ca saptamīm vyācakṣate tacca sarvaṃ nopayogyuktayojane

plain_english: And what is shown is not false nor mind-confusing; this true reality of departure is from Shri Shambhunatha.
sanskrit_cite: naca taddarśitaṃ mithyā svāntasammohadāyakam taditthaṃprāyaṇasyaitattattvaṃ śrīśambhunāthataḥ

plain_english: By that, fear of death perishes; knowing death's true reality, nectar arises from the consciousness treasury; if gods drink when poison is swallowed here, then your Shiva-nature is certain.
sanskrit_cite: adhigamyoditaṃ tena mṛtyorbhītirvinaśyati viditamṛtisatattvāḥ saṃvidambhonidhānādacalahṛdayavīryākarṣaniṣpīḍanottham amṛtamiti nigīrṇe kālakūṭe@tra devā yadi pivatha tadānīṃ niścitaṃ vaḥ śivatvam

plain_english: Even a worldly festival indeed produces joy resembling waves of the consciousness ocean; that too is like a parvan.
sanskrit_cite: utsavo@pi hi yaḥ kaścillaukikaḥ so@pi saṃmadam saṃvidabdhitaraṅgābhaṃ sūte tadapi parvavat

plain_english: By this, parvans are explained in disaster, destruction, joy, and so on; by that, deity worship is especially important there too.
sanskrit_cite: etena ca vipaddhvaṃsapramodādiṣu parvatā vyākhyātā tena tatrāpi viśeṣāddevatārcanam

plain_english: The wonder from city agitation gives firmness to one's own consciousness in self-power; special worship is on the day of its gain.

plain_english: The yogini assembly is twofold, by force and by love; holes are protected in the east, desire-conduct in the north.
sanskrit_cite: yoginīmelako dvedhā haṭhataḥ priyatastathā prācye cchidrāṇi saṃrakṣetkāmacāritvamuttare

plain_english: By that, that parvan and likewise union of one's own lineage etc.; consciousness is all-self, but she contracts in body difference etc.
sanskrit_cite: tena tatparva tadvacca svasantānādimelanam saṃvitsarvātmikā dehabhedādyā saṅkucettu sā

plain_english: In assembly, blooming from mutual collision reflection, the rising flood of one's own rays is reflected in consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: melake@nyonyasaṅghaṭṭapratibimbādvikasvarā ucchalannijaraśmyoghaḥ saṃvitsu pratibimbitaḥ

plain_english: Shining like many mirrors, effortlessly for all; therefore in song and the like, in a large assembly.
sanskrit_cite: bahudarpaṇavaddīptaḥ sarvāyetāpyayatnataḥ ata eva gītagītaprabhṛtau bahuparṣadi

plain_english: The delight in the all-pervading state is not of one alone; bliss-full consciousness is for each, and she thus attains unity.

plain_english: The blooming, unobstructed consciousness-bliss yogini is obstructed in a non-pervading state when something stays there.
sanskrit_cite: vikasvarā niṣpratighaṃ saṃvidānandayoginī atanmaye tu kasmiṃścittatrasthe pratihanyate

plain_english: When established by consciousness of a different kind, like touching a cavity, therefore in wheel worship and the like, different-kind non-pervading matter is relevant.

plain_english: Indeed one should not introduce the cause of consciousness contraction; as many bodies as limbs would be fully filled.
sanskrit_cite: naiva praveśayetsaṃvitsaṅkocananibandhanam yāvantyeva śarīrāṇi svāṅgavatsyuḥ sunirbharām

plain_english: Having entered one consciousness in the wheel, one should worship that many; if entered by negligence, contraction should not follow from that.
sanskrit_cite: ekāṃ saṃvidamāviśya cakre tāvanti pūjayet praviṣṭaścetpramādena saṅkocaṃ na vrajettataḥ

plain_english: Commenced own conduct should be practiced together by that; if pierced by your grace power, he becomes that-pervading.

plain_english: The left-pierced one, however, should be blamed afterwards and even struck; as said at first in Shrimat Picuma, protect with effort.
sanskrit_cite: vāmāviddhastu tannindetpaścāttaṃ ghātayedapi śrīmatpicumate coktamādau yatnena rakṣayet

plain_english: For one who has entered, inquiry should not be caused; but one established in worldly conduct, when such a one has entered, he is that.

plain_english: Without omitting that observance, one should worship the circle again. Now I will speak of the stated order for the teacher's explanation of scripture.
sanskrit_cite: akṛtvā taṃ samācāraṃ punaścakraṃ prapūjayet atha vacmi guroḥ śāstravyākhyākramamudāhṛtam

plain_english: In the Devīyāmala and related scriptures, the moon-crested Lord describes one who knows ritual procedure and its collections, one who knows scripture, and one who knows the meaning of the compendia.

sanskrit_cite: sarvaśāstrārthavicceti gururbhinno@padiśyate yo yatra śāstre svabhyastajñāno vyākhyāṃ carettu saḥ

plain_english: It should not be done otherwise. But if such a qualified person is entirely unavailable, even then one may act differently. In the revered Bhairava lineage, such knowledge of ritual procedure and the rest is also described.

plain_english: The mark of a teacher is simply complete knowledge. Yet even that knowledge has inner divisions, according to the differing activities of consciousness.

plain_english: Ucchuṣma, Śavara, Caṇḍa, Gumataṅga, Ghora, Antaka, Ugra, Hala, Halaka, Krodhin, and Huluhulu—these are the ten ancient teachers, all consisting of Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: ucchuṣmaśavaracaṇḍagumataṅgaghorāntakograhalahalakāḥ krodhī huluhulurete daśa guravaḥ śivamayāḥ pūrve

plain_english: By the sequence of their own partial modes of consciousness, they assume human bodies. Though their awareness and activity differ from one another, they are all full of knowledge.

plain_english: All of them are devoted to the service of meat, wine, union, initiation, worship, and scripture. Their inner difference lies in qualities such as pride, calm, anger, and forbearance.

plain_english: Having understood this, the wise student should always request a teacher who knows the complete scripture to give an explanation, doing so with worship beforehand.

plain_english: The teacher should give an explanation of such a scripture to his own student, or even to another's student, if the person is fit to hear it—even to a Vaiṣṇava or someone of a lower affiliation.
sanskrit_cite: so@pi svaśāsanīye paraśiṣye@pivāpi tādṛśaṃ śāstram śrotuṃ yogye kuryādvyākhyānaṃ vaiṣṇavādyadhare

plain_english: A teacher filled with compassion may explain even to a low person, while avoiding the vital secret matters, because the descent of power can occur in many different ways.

plain_english: On a smeared, square seat on the ground, one should make three lotuses. On the lotus, one should make the seat of knowledge, measuring six and three finger-widths.

plain_english: In the middle one should worship Vāgīśānī; on the south and north, the teachers and Gaṇeśa; and on the lower lotus, the lord of the ritual tradition, using offering water, flowers, and libations.

plain_english: Using the offering vessel as in the general rite, the wise teacher should properly satisfy the circle and then give the explanation, beginning with the proper connection.

plain_english: By connecting aphorism, word, sentence, chapter, and the whole text in order, and by supporting an unbroken link between what comes before and after, one should lead the sentences forward.
sanskrit_cite: sūtrapadavākyapaṭalagranthakramayojanena sambandhāt avyāhatapūrvāparamupavṛhya nayeta vākyāni

plain_english: Using principles such as the frog-leap and the lion-glance as appropriate, one should present the meaning of the scripture clearly, without mixing it up and without breaking the link between what comes before and after.

plain_english: One who understands sentences should explain the subject using sound reasoning—such as repetition, contradiction, unwanted consequence, and inference—while keeping it clearly distinct from other matters.

plain_english: Whatever point comes up in the explanation should be supported with very firm reasoning, even if it is something that will later be refuted.

plain_english: When the subject is taught by first setting out a firmly formed prior view and then resolving it, it quickly enters the student's mind, free from doubt and misunderstanding.
sanskrit_cite: dṛḍharacitapūrvapakṣaproddharaṇapathena vastu yadvācyam śiṣyamatāvārohati tadāśu saṃśayaviparyayairvikalam

plain_english: Whatever language, reasoning, style of discussion, level of absorption, or order becomes a means of awakening for the student, the teacher should adopt that form of explanation.
sanskrit_cite: bhāṣā nyāyo vādo layaḥ kramo yadyadeti śiṣyasya sambodhopāyatvaṃ tathaiva gururāśrayedvyākhyām

plain_english: After completing the subject being explained, there should be satisfaction and worship in the circle. Another subject may be taught after a chapter, but there should be no idle talk.

plain_english: At the end of the explanation, one should ask forgiveness, dismiss everything, and cast the remains into deep water. Worship should be performed especially at the beginning, middle, and end of the scripture.

plain_english: At the completion, one should perform special worship for the initiates. Even so, for one whose mind is undivided, there may be no need for expiations.

plain_english: Even so, for the grace of those who do not know the truth, one should act as taught in the revered Picu scripture. But if remembrance alone destroys sin, O Lord, how can an expiation rite still be prescribed?
