plain_english: When the Goddess asked why an expiation rite is declared, the answer is: it is true that remembrance alone, even uttered once, can liberate one here.
sanskrit_cite: prāyaścittavidhiḥ prokta iti devyā pracodite satyaṃ smaraṇameveha sakṛjjaptaṃ vimocayet

plain_english: For one who knows remembrance and its truth, liberation from the whole net of action is possible; nevertheless, the rite is enjoined as something to be done for the protection of order.
sanskrit_cite: sarvasmātkarmaṇo jālātsmṛtitattvakalāvidaḥ tathāpi sthitirakṣārthaṃ kartavyaścodito vidhiḥ

plain_english: Those who do not know the truth and are devoted only to ritual conduct suffer a loss of knowledge when their minds begin to waver.
sanskrit_cite: atattvavedino ye hi caryāmātraikaniṣṭhitāḥ teṣāṃ dolāyite citte jñānahāniḥ prajāyate

plain_english: Therefore, if one is free from doubt, one should remain discreet and avoid causing confusion when among those who depend on scripture and ritual conduct.
sanskrit_cite: tasmādvikalparahitaḥ saṃvṛtyuparato yadi śāstracaryāsadāyattaiḥ saṅkaraṃ tadvivarjayet

plain_english: If confusion of practice arises, one should seek and perform expiation, so that the minds of others do not become unsteady about the meaning of scripture.
sanskrit_cite: saṅkaraṃ vā samanvicchetprāyaścittaṃ samācaret yathā teṣāṃ na śāstrārthe dolārūḍhā matirbhavet

plain_english: In the rite called Shiva-hand it was formerly enjoined that, by reciting this weapon mantra a hundred times, one is freed, except in the case of killing a woman.
sanskrit_cite: yatsvayaṃ śivahastākhye vidhau saṃcoditaṃ purā śataṃ japtvāsya cāstrasya mucyate strīvadhādṛte

plain_english: The revered Ratnamala says, O beloved, that when a vow is transgressed, the destruction of a woman is a great fault leading to everlasting hell.
sanskrit_cite: śaktināśānmahādoṣo narakaṃ śāśvataṃ priye iti śrīratnamālāyāṃ samayollaṅghane kṛte

plain_english: For those born in the Kula, an expiation called the wicked knife has been declared; and in the revered earlier text, a purification of the vows is enjoined as follows.
sanskrit_cite: kulajānāṃ samākhyātā niṣkṛtirduṣṭakartarī śrīpūrve samayānāṃ tu śodhanāyoditaṃ yathā

plain_english: If an installed sacred object and the like is seen by someone without authority, Malini or Matrika should be recited, up to three hundred thousand times.
sanskrit_cite: mālinī mātṛkā vāpi japyā lakṣatrayāntakam pratiṣṭhitasya pūrāderdarśane@nadhikāriṇā

plain_english: In the revered Brahmayamala it is said that expiation must be performed by a killer of a brahmin, by one who violates the guru's bed, and likewise by one who steals the hero-substance.
sanskrit_cite: prāyaścittaṃ prakartavyamiti śrībrahmayāmale brahmaghno gurutalpastho vīradravyaharastathā

plain_english: Also included are one who takes the property of the gods or strikes a sacred form, one who breaks the linga, and one who neglects the daily rites and has fallen from his proper measure and equipment.
sanskrit_cite: devadravyahṛdākāraprahartā liṅgabhedakaḥ nityādilopakṛdbhraṣṭasvakamātrāparicchadaḥ

plain_english: One who maims Shakti or kills a yogin or knower, or who disrupts the occasional rites, should recite in a doubling sequence beginning with a hundred thousand.
sanskrit_cite: śaktivyaṅgatvakṛdyogijñānihantā vilopakaḥ naimittikānāṃ lakṣādikramāddvidviguṇaṃ japet

plain_english: If someone under a vow, eating moderately and observing celibacy, goes elsewhere to take a messenger woman, deluded by desire, that is an offense.
sanskrit_cite: vratena kenacidyukto mitabhugbrahmacaryavān dūtīparigrahe@nyatra gataścetkāmamohitaḥ

plain_english: Then one should perform a recitation of a hundred thousand, as stated in the Brahmayamala; and at the end of initiation, consecration, and occasional rites, worship of the guru is required.
sanskrit_cite: lakṣajāpaṃ tataḥ kuryādityuktaṃ brahmayāmale dīkṣābhiṣekanaimittavidhyante gurupūjanam

plain_english: According to the teaching of the Siddhayogishvari, it should always be done on the next day: worship of a guru endowed with the previously stated marks, a seer who knows the true principle of the Trika.
sanskrit_cite: aparedyuḥ sadā kāryaṃ siddhayogīśvarīmate pūrvoktalakṣaṇopetaḥ kavistrikasatattvavit

plain_english: That guru should always be accepted, leaving aside any other, even one present in the circle. One should make a svastika there and place upon it a golden or similar seat.
sanskrit_cite: sa guruḥ sarvadā grāhyastyaktvānyaṃ tatsthitaṃ tvapi maṇḍale svastikaṃ kṛtvā tatra haimādikāsanam

plain_english: Having prepared the seat, one should worship the path present there in its full extent; then, with devotion, one should request the guru to preside there.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtvārcayeta tatrasthamadhvānaṃ sakalāntakam tato vijñapayedbhaktyā tadadhiṣṭhitaye gurum

plain_english: There he should be worshiped with his own mantras, in due order, with flowers, incense, arghya, respectful touching, fine garments, food offerings, and libations.
sanskrit_cite: sa tatra pūjyaḥ svairmantraiḥ puṣpadhūpārghavistaraiḥ samālambhanasadvastrairnaivedyaistarpaṇaiḥ kramāt

plain_english: After worshiping him fully, even to the directions, the disciple should honor him with gifts, offering all he has and, with devout awareness, even himself.
sanskrit_cite: āśāntaṃ pūjayitvainaṃ dakṣiṇābhiryajecchiśuḥ sarvasvamasmai saṃdadyādātmānamapi bhāvitaḥ

plain_english: By fully satisfying the guru with gifts, even one who knows the truth is freed from the bond of debt and thereby attains proper fitness for authority.
sanskrit_cite: atoṣayitvā tu guruṃ dakṣiṇābhiḥ samantataḥ tattvajño@pyṛṇabandhena tena yātyadhikāritām

plain_english: According to the Skandayamala, one who does not perform guru worship is born for a hundred lifetimes and only then becomes fit for authority and attains liberation.
sanskrit_cite: gurupūjāmakurvāṇaḥ śataṃ janmāni jāyate adhikārī tato muktiṃ yātīti skandayāmale

plain_english: Therefore a gift must certainly be given again to the guru: earlier it was declared as part of the rite, but this giving is for his satisfaction.
sanskrit_cite: tasmādavaśyaṃ dātavyā gurave dakṣiṇā punaḥ pūrvaṃ hi yāgāṅgatayā proktaṃ tattuṣṭaye tvidam

plain_english: Then, having received his permission, the disciple may partake of what the guru has accepted; after that, he should worship the circle according to the resources available.
sanskrit_cite: tajjuṣṭamatha tasyājñāṃ prāpyāśnīyātsvayaṃ śiśuḥ tataḥ prapūjayeccakraṃ yathāvibhavasambhavam

plain_english: Without performing the teacher sacrifice, even completed rites remain undone; therefore the teacher sacrifice must be performed diligently according to one's strength.
sanskrit_cite: akṛtvā guruyāgaṃ tu kṛtamapyakṛtaṃ yataḥ tasmātprayatnataḥ kāryo guruyāgo yathābalam

plain_english: Even if the teacher stays there, he is worshipful; having resolved as before, that substance should be used in the deity rite for devotees.
sanskrit_cite: atatrastho@pi hi guruḥ pūjyaḥ saṃkalpya pūrvavat taddravyaṃ devatākṛtye kuryādbhaktajaneṣvatha

plain_english: This rite is occasional, distinguished by parva, pavitra, and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: parvapavitraprabhṛtiprabhedi naimittikaṃ tvidaṃ karma
